title: What the thread body needs
prompt: To move a loop body into its own C function, you need the names it uses but doesn't define: those travel in the context struct. A body is a list of statements (name, uses), in order. Write free_vars(body, loop_var): the names used in the body that are not defined in it and are not loop_var (the function's own argument), sorted, without repeats.
hints: Collect the defined names first: every name in the body.
A use is free when it isn't defined in the body and isn't loop_var.
Use a set to drop repeats, then sorted.
explain: This is closure conversion, the step every compiler takes when it turns a nested block into a separate function. In the rendered C, b0 (a buffer), v0 (a value computed before the loop) and enclosing ranges like r3 are free in the body, so they go into the struct. Names the body defines, like private allocs and its own values, are declared inside the function instead.
